title: Deep learning predicts COVID-19 mortality from routine labs in a large health-record set
summary: A GRU-D recurrent neural network (with AutoGluon stacked learners) predicted COVID-19 mortality within 72 hours of the first positive test from routine laboratory results and covariates in 11,807 Mayo Clinic patients. Cross-validation AUROC was 0.938 and a prospective testing cohort gave AUROC 0.901 with significantly different survival between risk groups. The data come from a single health system in 2020-21 and the abstract does not give the prospective cohort size.
ai_technology: GRU-D recurrent neural network and AutoGluon stacked learners on laboratory and covariate time series

evidence.tested: Cross-validation in 11,807 patients plus a prospective testing cohort at the Mayo Clinic.
evidence.unknown: Prospective cohort size; performance outside this health system and later pandemic periods; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A recurrent neural network predicted mortality from irregularly sampled routine laboratory data.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
